data.narrative: Ran a system-level security & architecture review of every AI-generated endpoint across Modules 02-06 (auth map, input validation audit, IDOR check, secrets/dependency audit, pattern consistency). Found 3 critical/high/medium findings (comment IDOR, expired-link redirect, /audit PII over-exposure) and closed them with fixes plus a security regression suite. The privilege-escalation vector from BREAK was traced end-to-end and confirmed already closed in this codebase (require_owner + role enum), then pinned with an 11-test threat model covering the full viewer/member/admin/owner matrix.

dimension_scores.observation: Applied the module's fix-prompt discipline: instead of 'fix the role endpoint', enumerated six explicit constraints (owner/admin gate, self-modification block, role enum, admin-cannot-promote-to-owner, audit entry, tests) and translated them into a concrete regression suite.
dimension_scores.evidence: test_module7_role_escalation.py: 11 tests covering viewer/member/admin/owner matrix plus superadmin/empty/uppercase role rejection.

dimension_scores.observation: Built a complete endpoint map (auth + authorization per route), input validation audit, IDOR check, secrets audit, dependency audit, and cross-team access tests. Caught the combination-check lesson the module teaches: permission checks must verify the RIGHT permission, not just ANY permission.
dimension_scores.evidence: module-07-security-review.md: 30+ endpoints mapped; F1 comment IDOR (CRITICAL), F2 expired-link redirect (HIGH), F3 /audit PII exposure (MEDIUM) found and fixed with regression tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Each finding was closed with one targeted patch and a regression test; the privilege escalation was confirmed already closed by tracing all three role-write paths rather than patching blindly.
dimension_scores.evidence: module-07-break-trace.md: three role-write paths enumerated (add_member require_owner_or_admin, update_member_role require_owner, accept_invitation ROLE_MEMBER) - vector does not exist; no iteration spiral.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose AI-assisted hybrid (decision B) with the human critical-path review focused on authn/authz role checks - the exact spot the module says the scanner's blind spot lives (scanner sees isTeamMember and marks it protected without checking the RIGHT permission level).
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE module_07 choice B: 'AI scan for volume brute-force pass... manual review time on the critical path: authn/authz role checks, data mutation call chains.'

dimension_scores.observation: Shipped the audit as a living checklist document (module-07-security-review.md), closed all critical/high findings, and left the privilege-escalation threat model pinned by automated tests - the exact protection the module demands.
dimension_scores.evidence: 31 tests green (test_teams + test_module7_role_escalation); test_module7_security.py regression suite green.

strengths: Traced the privilege-escalation vector through all three role-write code paths and proved it cannot exist (require_owner is stricter than the canonical membership-check pattern, role field is enum-validated).
Caught and fixed the comment IDOR (CRITICAL) with a DB-backed owner guard and live probes showing 404 for foreign users.
Closed the /audit PII over-exposure (invitee emails visible to plain members) by scoping team entries to owner/admin, matching the scoped endpoint.
Converted the module's 13-case threat model into an 11-test automated regression suite rather than a one-time manual check.
growth_areas: Freeze the check-composition habit: the module's core lesson is that permission presence (isTeamMember) is not permission correctness (isAdminOrOwner) - codify the 'verify the RIGHT permission, not just ANY permission' rule as the first line of every future auth review.
data.recommendation: Add the updated security checklist (auth map, input validation, IDOR, secrets, cross-team, self-modification, right-permission, role enum, deps, auth boundary tests) as a reusable review checklist file and reuse it verbatim on every future AI-generated codebase in Module 08.
